title: Xanthe and the Summit
premise: Ansel Dravenmoor, the last riverboat captain willing to run the Vell, is hired to find a survey expedition that went silent near the river's forbidden source — a headwater her own father died trying to chart twenty years ago. Among the missing is Ilya Marchetti, the cartographer she once loved and lost to duty's call upstream. As Ansel fights rapids, sabotage from a mining syndicate that wants the source uncharted, and her own buried grief, she discovers the expedition survivors hiding in an abandoned mission, hunted by men who will drown the valley rather than let it be mapped. In the end Ansel must choose between saving the maps that would protect the river forever and saving Ilya, and she finds a third way: burning the syndicate's claim while letting the river keep its secret, at the cost of the life she built below.
about_author: Wendell Villalobos spent a decade piloting supply boats on remote tributaries before turning to fiction, and his prose carries the smell of diesel and rain. He writes from a stilt house on a river he refuses to name, where he keeps his late father's waterlogged charts framed above the desk.

chapters.title: The Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Ansel pilots the Marguerite through a dying-season drought, establishing her intimate knowledge of the Vell and her solitary life after her father's death. A telegram arrives: the Corvus Survey has gone silent, and the company wants her — because only she knows the old smuggler's channel past the Falls of Ket. POV: Ansel. Beat: restless competence masking grief; duty knocking at a door she nailed shut.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Reviewing the expedition's manifest, Ansel finds Ilya Marchetti's name and floods with memory of their love and his choice of the survey over her. She almost refuses the job, but the company's offer includes clearing her father's posthumous disgrace — he was branded a liar for claiming a source no one found. POV: Ansel, with flashback passages. Beat: old love resurfacing as both wound and bait.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Clock
chapters.summary: Ansel takes on a skeleton crew — gruff engineer Boaz and runaway deckhand Tilly — and begins the ascent, racing the dry season that will strand any boat above the narrows. First signs of trouble: cut telegraph lines and a burned waystation that was torched, not abandoned. POV: Ansel. Beat: dread accumulating; the wilderness turns from home to adversary.

chapters.title: What the Rapids Keep
chapters.summary: Running the Falls of Ket by night, the Marguerite nearly founders; Tilly is nearly lost, and Ansel saves her in a sequence that mirrors how her father died. Among flotsam they recover a survey case containing Ilya's field journal, its last pages describing men following them who 'want the river blind.' POV: Ansel, intercut with Ilya's journal voice. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; the enemy acquires a face.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Silence
chapters.summary: At a trading post, Ansel confronts a representative of the Halvard Consolidated Mining Company, which holds concessions contingent on the source remaining officially undiscovered. He offers her triple pay to turn back and hints her father took the same bribe and refused it. POV: Ansel. Beat: temptation made explicit; she understands now what killed him.

chapters.title: Smoke Above the Mission
chapters.summary: Following Ilya's journal to the ruined San Vered mission, Ansel finds three starving survivors and learns the rest were killed in an ambush staged as an accident. Ilya is not among them — he went ahead alone toward the source to finish the map. POV: Ansel, plus survivor testimony. Beat: hope and horror braided together; the rescue becomes a race.

chapters.title: The Narrows of Ket
chapters.summary: Halvard's hired gunboats close the river behind them. Ansel runs the Marguerite through the unmapped narrows using her father's secret charts, sacrificing the boat's hull and half their supplies to slip past the blockade. Boaz is wounded covering the escape. POV: Ansel. Beat: the price of survival becomes literal; no going back now.

chapters.title: Where the River Is Born
chapters.summary: On foot, Ansel reaches the source — a cathedral cavern springing from living rock — and finds Ilya alive, guarding his finished map, half-mad with isolation and guilt over the deaths. Their reunion is furious and tender; he begs her to take the map out, knowing it will doom whoever carries it. POV: alternating Ansel and Ilya. Beat: love against duty made flesh; both must choose.

chapters.title: The Drowning Men
chapters.summary: Halvard's gunners arrive to destroy the cavern and bury all witnesses. In the climax, Ansel collapses the approach gorge with the expedition's blasting stores, drowning the gunboats' route and sealing the source behind a wall of flood — but Ilya is caught in the torrent saving Tilly, and Ansel dives after him into the white water. POV: Ansel. Beat: climax; survival demanded at its cruelest price.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Ansel drags Ilya's body ashore alive but broken, and they drift the wounded home on a raft, carrying nothing out of the headwaters but each other. The company discredits her account; her father's name stays disgraced; yet the source remains unmapped and safe, and she and Ilya choose the river over every claim upon them. POV: Ansel. Beat: bittersweet resolution — memory kept, duty paid, love chosen at cost.
